RSI & MACD Indicators
Support & Resistance Levels

Support and resistance are analyst-selected areas where past prices have stopped falling or rising. They are not physical barriers or proof of participant intent. Choice of lookback, tolerance and chart scale affects where they are drawn.

💡
Example

Hypothetical closes touch 100, rise to 104, return to 100, then close at 97. Two earlier observations near 100 might motivate a support annotation, but the final observation breaks it. Whether a later return to 100 is called resistance must be checked on later data; it is not an automatic role reversal.

Write the rule before looking at the next observation.
Record failed levels as well as apparent successful reactions.
Compare a zone with a precise line; changing tolerance after the result can overfit the story.
Pro Tip

A drawn level does not place an order. Gaps, execution costs and missing liquidity can make the practice assumption differ from a real fill.

One rumor is not three independent sources

Decision habits · 2026-11-14

Read the case first. Use its assumptions; these are not live market prices.

Close case
Case briefing and follow-up situation

Three hypothetical social posts repeat the same anonymous rumor about a company. All link back to the same original post, and none cites a company filing. Counting the reposts as independent confirmation exaggerates the evidence. Trace the source chain before using popularity as a reason for a simulated decision.

Draw the source chain as one anonymous origin feeding three reposts. Now suppose a fourth message repeats the same claim but provides no new source, while a separate company document is located but says nothing about the rumor. Trace which items add independent information and which merely repeat or fail to address the claim. A primary document’s existence alone is not confirmation of every allegation.
